title: Choose the visual world for HomeStage
question: The roll assigned the modernist furniture catalogue. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Catalogue No. 07
options.lineage: 1950s modernist furniture catalogues and spec sheets
options.thesis: Every product is a numbered plate in a furniture catalogue, with the spec sheet as the selling page.
options.viewport: An open catalogue spread: left page a full ochre colour plate with the sofa and its plate number; right page the model name, front/side/plan drawings with dimensions, the fabric range as numbered plates, price, Add to cart and Order a sample.
options.risk: Reads as retro pastiche if the grid goes loose or the plates go pale.

raised.raise: Order a sample is the test strip: sampling is shown as the step before committing, beside Add to cart, never a footnote link.
Lead time is staged as the making itself (frame, springs, upholstery, finishing), not one 'ships in 8 weeks' line.
Selection rides the material: choosing a fabric repaints the plate's colour field instead of drawing a ring around a chip.
One body size does the work; hierarchy comes from the grid and the plates, not a ladder of type sizes.
A fabric change dissolves the plate as one continuous transition, never an image swap.
One monumental typographic event per phone screen: the model name, set once, very large.

options.label: The Sample Book
options.thesis: The page opens like the fabric book in a showroom: you choose the cloth first, then the sofa.
options.viewport: A fan of numbered swatch cards across the top; picking one recolours the sofa photo and the page ground below it, with price, lead time and Order this swatch.
options.risk: Familiar: swatch-first pages are where many furniture redesigns land.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: The product develops in front of you, station by station.
options.viewport: An amber field where the sofa image develops as you scroll.
options.case: Fuses poorly: furniture owners do not identify with a darkroom; amber hides true fabric colour.
options.risk: Colour-accurate swatches are impossible under safelight.
options.kept: The test strip: sample before you commit.

options.label: Raku Smoke Flash
options.thesis: Making as a staged, unrepeatable firing.
options.viewport: A soot-black field with the product as a fired vessel.
options.case: Fuses poorly for sofas; closer for the ceramics page only.
options.risk: Dark ground fights fabric colour and family-living mood.
options.kept: Lead time staged as the making itself.

options.label: Op-art Gallery
options.thesis: Flat black-and-white fields that move as you look.
options.viewport: A white room of wave paintings with the sofa in it.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no colour means no fabric story.
options.risk: Moiré on product photos reads as a rendering fault.
options.kept: State rides the material, not chrome.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: The product as a tabbed manual with acetate overlays.
options.viewport: Tabbed sections for fabric, size and delivery.
options.case: Fuses poorly: reads as software, not furniture.
options.risk: Feels like documentation to a shopper.
options.kept: One body size does the work.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.viewport: Letters forming the product name as weather.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hides the product behind type.
options.risk: No room for photos, swatches or dimensions.
options.kept: One monumental type moment per screen.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.thesis: A living GPU scene with thin type floating over it.
options.viewport: A full-screen shader with the product floating inside.
options.case: Fuses poorly: heavy on phones and against Theme Store speed rules.
options.risk: Slow, and nothing a home brand could actually use.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The online furniture product page every shopper expects, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Photo gallery left, name, price, round swatches and Add to cart right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every furniture store by design.
